creator: NASA image created by Jesse Allen, Earth Observatory, using data obtained from the MODIS Rapid Response team.
alt: An archival satellite image of Typhoon Nanmadol, used to illustrate tropical-cyclone structure rather than a current warning.
description: The MODIS instrument onboard NASA's Terra satellite captured this true-color image of Typhoon Nanmadol at 02:00 UTC on December 1, 2004. At the time this image was taken Nanmadol was located approximately 390 miles west-northwest of Yap and was moving at a brisk 28 mph towards the west-northwest. Maximum sustained winds were near 120 mph with higher gusts to 150 mph. NASA image created by Jesse Allen, Earth Observatory, using data obtained from the MODIS Rapid Response team.
caption: An archival satellite image of Typhoon Nanmadol, used to illustrate tropical-cyclone structure rather than a current warning.

creator: NASA astronaut Ed Lu
alt: The eye of Hurricane Isabel photographed from the International Space Station in 2003, shown as historical tropical-cyclone structure context.
description: NASA astronaut Ed Lu took this image of the eye of Hurricane Isabel from the International Space Station at 11:18 UTC on September 13, 2003. At the time of the image, Isabel had weakened to a Category 4 hurricane on the Saffir-Simpson Hurricane Scale, from its peak as a Category 5. The storm was located about 450 miles northeast of Puerto Rico. The camera used was a Kodak DCS760C electronic still camera with a focal length of 180 mm.
caption: The eye of Hurricane Isabel photographed from the International Space Station in 2003, shown as historical tropical-cyclone structure context.
